```{r setup}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

root <- normalizePath("..")   # Quarto runs chunks from analysis/
for (f in list.files(file.path(root, "R"), full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

sim <- readRDS(file.path(root, "analysis", "results", "simulation_results.rds"))
```

## How the recommendations are chosen

A cleaning method is only useful if it removes contamination **without
removing real biology**. So the rule is explicit and applied to the
simulation results from [Part 2](02_simulation_study.html), using only the
scenarios with realistic (leaky) negative controls:

1. Discard every method/threshold that, on average, removes more than **1% of
   genuine reads** or more than **2 genuine taxa** (out of 150).
2. Among the rest, pick the one that removes the most contamination.

The thresholds are a judgement call, written down so they can be argued
with. They reflect a typical clinical priority: losing a real organism is
worse than leaving some contamination that can be flagged in the report.

```{r rule}
max_reads_lost <- 1
max_taxa_lost <- 2

cand <- sim$results |>
  filter(leak > 0) |>
  mutate(choice = ifelse(is.na(threshold), method,
                         paste0(method, " ", threshold))) |>
  group_by(conc_noise, biomass_ratio, n_neg, choice) |>
  summarise(removed = mean(contam_reads_removed),
            reads_lost = mean(true_reads_lost),
            taxa_lost = mean(true_taxa_lost), .groups = "drop")

best <- cand |>
  filter(reads_lost <= max_reads_lost, taxa_lost <= max_taxa_lost) |>
  group_by(conc_noise, biomass_ratio, n_neg) |>
  slice_max(removed, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

stopifnot(nrow(best) == nrow(distinct(cand, conc_noise, biomass_ratio, n_neg)))
```

## Recommendation table

Each cell shows the best method and threshold, and the share of
contamination it removes on average.

```{r rec-table}
best |>
  mutate(
    Quantification = ifelse(conc_noise == 0.1, "Precise", "Imprecise"),
    Biomass = factor(biomass_ratio, levels = c(100, 10, 1),
                     labels = c("High (~1% contam.)", "Low (~6%)",
                                "Very low (~40%)")),
    cell = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", choice, removed),
    n_neg = paste(n_neg, ifelse(n_neg == 1, "control", "controls"))
  ) |>
  select(Quantification, Biomass, n_neg, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = n_neg, values_from = cell) |>
  arrange(desc(Quantification), Biomass) |>
  kable(align = "llllll")

share_freq <- mean(grepl("^frequency", best$choice))
low_imprecise <- best |> filter(conc_noise == 0.5, biomass_ratio == 1)

# Where another method wins, how far behind is the best frequency option?
passing <- cand |>
  filter(reads_lost <= max_reads_lost, taxa_lost <= max_taxa_lost)
gap <- best |>
  filter(!grepl("^frequency", choice)) |>
  left_join(passing |>
              filter(grepl("^frequency", choice)) |>
              group_by(conc_noise, biomass_ratio, n_neg) |>
              summarise(best_freq = max(removed), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("conc_noise", "biomass_ratio", "n_neg")) |>
  mutate(gap = removed - best_freq)
n_05_pass <- sum(grepl(" 0.5$", passing$choice))
```

What the table says:

* **The frequency method is the backbone.** It is the selected method in
  `r round(100 * share_freq)`% of the designs. Where a method that also uses
  the negative controls wins, the best frequency option is on average
  `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(gap$gap))` percentage points behind (at most
  `r sprintf("%.1f", max(gap$gap))`). Leaked DNA in the controls is what
  stops those methods from doing better: push their thresholds up and they
  start removing real taxa.
* **Thresholds of 0.1–0.25 are the safe range.** A threshold of 0.5 passes
  the "don't remove real biology" rule in `r n_05_pass` of the
  `r nrow(passing |> distinct(conc_noise, biomass_ratio, n_neg))` designs.
* **Very low biomass plus imprecise quantification cannot be fixed in
  software.** The best option there removes only
  `r round(min(low_imprecise$removed))`–`r round(max(low_imprecise$removed))`%
  of the contamination. The fix is upstream: better DNA quantification, more
  starting material, or reporting the data as exploratory.

## Decision guide

The flowchart condenses the table above for a single sample type.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A["One sample type<br/>with its own negative controls"] --> B{"DNA measured precisely?<br/>(fluorometric or qPCR)"}
    B -- Yes --> C["decontam frequency<br/>threshold 0.1 to 0.25"]
    B -- No --> D{"Very low biomass?<br/>(e.g. blood, ascitic fluid)"}
    D -- No --> E["decontam frequency, threshold 0.1<br/>expect partial cleaning"]
    D -- Yes --> F["No method cleans reliably:<br/>report residual contamination<br/>and treat results as exploratory"]
    C --> G["Checks: no abundant taxon removed,<br/>threshold and reads removed reported"]
    E --> G
    F --> G
```

Three rules hold in every scenario:

1. **Do not remove every taxon found in the negative controls.** It removed
   real taxa in the mock community (Part 1) and most genuine reads in the
   simulations (Part 2).
2. **Clean each sample type separately**, against its own controls: contamination is a larger share of
   blood than of a swab, so the evidence differs.
3. **Report the decision**, not just the result: method, threshold, number of
   taxa removed and share of reads removed per sample.

## Worked example: two sample types in one study

A simulated study with swabs (low biomass, precise quantification) and blood
(very low biomass, imprecise quantification, shallow sequencing), each with
four negative controls, cleaned with `clean_low_biomass()`. Because it is
simulated, we can check the result against the truth.

```{r example-data}
swab <- simulate_study(n_samples = 30, n_neg = 4, biomass_ratio = 10,
                       conc_noise = 0.1, leak = 0.005, seed = 2018)
blood <- simulate_study(n_samples = 30, n_neg = 4, biomass_ratio = 1,
                        conc_noise = 0.5, leak = 0.005,
                        depth_meanlog = log(6000), depth_sdlog = 0.8,
                        neg_depth_factor = 0.2, seed = 2019)
prefix <- function(s, p) {
  rownames(s$counts) <- s$samples$sample_id <- paste0(p, "_", s$samples$sample_id)
  s
}
swab <- prefix(swab, "SWAB")
blood <- prefix(blood, "BLOOD")

counts <- rbind(swab$counts, blood$counts)
samples <- rbind(cbind(swab$samples, sample_type = "swab"),
                 cbind(blood$samples, sample_type = "blood"))
expected <- setNames(swab$taxonomy$expected, swab$taxonomy$asv_id)
```

The settings follow the recommendation table: frequency method with
threshold 0.1, the fixed 1,000-read rule for swabs and the "median of the
controls" rule for blood.

```{r example-clean}
cleaned <- clean_low_biomass(
  counts, samples, group = "sample_type",
  method = "frequency",
  threshold = c(swab = 0.1, blood = 0.1),
  low_read_rule = c(swab = "fixed", blood = "neg_median"),
  min_reads = 1000
)

cleaned$summary |>
  select(-notes) |>
  rename(`Sample type` = group, Method = method, Threshold = threshold,
         `Read-depth rule` = read_rule, `Samples in` = samples_in,
         `Samples dropped` = samples_dropped, `Neg. controls` = negatives,
         `Taxa scored` = taxa_scored, `Taxa removed` = taxa_removed,
         `Median % reads removed` = median_pct_reads_removed) |>
  mutate(Threshold = format(Threshold, nsmall = 2)) |>
  kable(digits = 1)
```

### Checking against the truth

```{r example-truth, fig.height=4, fig.width=8}
#| fig-cap: "Contaminant share per sample before and after cleaning, by sample type. Every genuine taxon is known because the data are simulated."
kept_ids <- rownames(cleaned$counts)
before <- counts[kept_ids, ]
after <- cleaned$counts

truth <- tibble(
  sample_id = kept_ids,
  type = sub("_.*", "", kept_ids),
  Before = rowSums(before[, !expected]) / rowSums(before),
  After = rowSums(after[, !expected]) / rowSums(after),
  genuine_lost = 1 - rowSums(after[, expected]) / rowSums(before[, expected])
)

truth |>
  pivot_longer(c(Before, After), names_to = "stage", values_to = "contam") |>
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = c("Before", "After")),
         type = factor(type, levels = c("SWAB", "BLOOD"),
                       labels = c("Swab", "Blood"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(stage, contam, group = sample_id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.35, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = stage), size = 1.6) +
  facet_wrap(~type) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Before = "#BDBDBD", After = "#2C7FB8"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Contaminant share of reads")

by_type <- truth |>
  group_by(type) |>
  summarise(before = 100 * median(Before), after = 100 * median(After),
            lost = 100 * max(genuine_lost))
sw <- by_type[by_type$type == "SWAB", ]
bl <- by_type[by_type$type == "BLOOD", ]
```

In swabs, the median contaminant share fell from
`r sprintf("%.1f", sw$before)`% to `r sprintf("%.1f", sw$after)`%, with at
most `r sprintf("%.1f", sw$lost)`% of any sample's genuine reads removed. In
blood the median contaminant share was `r sprintf("%.0f", bl$before)`% before
cleaning and `r sprintf("%.0f", bl$after)`% after: exactly the situation the
guide flags as unfixable, and the reason the methods text below says so.

### Methods text, generated from the run

Reporting is part of the method. The paragraph below is written by the code
from `cleaned$summary`, so it always matches what was actually done:

```{r methods-text}
#| results: asis
s <- cleaned$summary
describe <- function(i) {
  sprintf(
    "%s samples (n = %d; %d negative controls) were cleaned with the decontam %s method (threshold %.2f) after excluding %d sample(s) under the %s read-depth rule; %d of %d scored taxa were classified as contaminants, removing a median of %.1f%% of reads per sample.",
    tools::toTitleCase(s$group[i]), s$samples_in[i], s$negatives[i], s$method[i],
    s$threshold[i], s$samples_dropped[i], s$read_rule[i], s$taxa_removed[i],
    s$taxa_scored[i], s$median_pct_reads_removed[i])
}
cat("> Contaminant sequences were identified separately for each sample type",
    "with decontam", as.character(packageVersion("decontam")),
    "(Davis et al., 2018), using DNA concentration measured before library",
    "preparation.", paste(vapply(seq_len(nrow(s)), describe, ""), collapse = " "),
    "Given the low biomass of the blood samples, residual contamination is",
    "expected and results for this sample type are reported as exploratory.\n")
```

## Summary: common practice and updated recommendation

| Common practice | Updated recommendation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Use decontam prevalence or frequency | Frequency first; prevalence only with clean, well-separated controls | Parts 1 and 2 |
| Threshold 0.1 or 0.5, often unreported | 0.1–0.25, chosen and reported | Part 2, Result 2 |
| Remove taxa dominant in controls | Allowed as a check, not as the main filter | Part 1 |
| NanoDrop concentration as input | Fluorometric or qPCR quantification | Part 2, Result 1 |
| 1,000 reads / median of controls | Kept, applied per sample type | Part 1 and this example |
| One sample type at a time | Kept | All parts |
